titleStmt.title: Current knowledge on exosome biogenesis and release
titleStmt.author: Nina P. Hessvik
Alicia Llorente

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Current knowledge on exosome biogenesis and release

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: how exosomes are formed and released - the intraluminal vesicles of the multivesicular body, and the transport and fusion steps that put them outside the cell
span.quote: Exosomes are nanosized membrane vesicles released by fusion of an organelle of the endocytic pathway, the multivesicular body, with the plasma membrane.

span.label: what is presently known about the molecular machinery of exosome biogenesis and release, and which of the steps the evidence can actually assign
span.quote: Several molecules have been implicated in these processes, but due to methodological challenges, it is not easy to distinguish them experimentally, and in many studies it is not clear at which step the investigated molecule/factor operates

span.label: a review of the biogenesis literature that is explicit about what its own methods cannot separate - including that the field's central term is routinely used for a centrifugation pellet
span.quote: It is also important to mention that the term “exosomes” is often used to refer to the pellet obtained after 100,000× g ultracentrifugation. Although this pellet is probably enriched in exosomes, it might also contain small microvesicles as well as protein aggregates.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Exosomes are nanosized membrane vesicles released by fusion of an organelle of the endocytic pathway, the multivesicular body, with the plasma membrane.

span.label: release of intraluminal vesicles into the extracellular space when a multivesicular body fuses with the plasma membrane - and the several other routes that yield something indistinguishable from it
span.quote: Furthermore, when amphisomes fuse with the plasma membrane, the ILVs included in the amphisome will appear extracellularly as exosomes. Also if a lysosome secretes its content before it is fully degraded, remaining ILVs can be released as exosomes.

span.label: narrative review of exosome biogenesis, transport and release, with a section on the methodological issues that might explain discrepant findings
span.term: narrative review of exosome biogenesis, transport and release, with a section on the methodological issues that might explain discrepant findings
span.quote: The discrepant findings might be due to cell-specific regulations, or due to methodological challenges, such as different protocols for isolation of vesicles and different methods to quantify the amount of released exosomes

span.label: early endosomes mature into multivesicular bodies whose membrane invaginates to form intraluminal vesicles; those ILVs become exosomes when the MVB fuses with the plasma membrane rather than with a lysosome
span.quote: Exosomes are nanosized membrane vesicles released by fusion of an organelle of the endocytic pathway, the multivesicular body, with the plasma membrane.

span.label: THE FATE DECISION IS THE MECHANISM AND IT IS THE LEAST KNOWN PART: an MVB can go to the lysosome for degradation or to the plasma membrane for release, and `little is known about the molecular mechanisms and the cellular statues that regulate this balance`
span.quote: Multivesicular bodies can either be directed to lysosomes where their content is degraded or transported to the plasma membrane for exosome release. Little is known about the molecular mechanisms and the cellular statues that regulate this balance.

span.label: AMPHISOMES AND LYSOSOMES PRODUCE THE SAME APPARENT OBJECT BY OTHER ROUTES: ILVs inside a fusing amphisome `will appear extracellularly as exosomes`, and a lysosome secreting before full degradation releases remaining ILVs `as exosomes`
span.quote: Furthermore, when amphisomes fuse with the plasma membrane, the ILVs included in the amphisome will appear extracellularly as exosomes. Also if a lysosome secretes its content before it is fully degraded, remaining ILVs can be released as exosomes.

span.label: THE TERM NAMES A CENTRIFUGE SETTING. `exosomes` is often used for the pellet obtained after 100,000x g ultracentrifugation, which `might also contain small microvesicles as well as protein aggregates` - a biogenesis word denoting an operation that does not implement it
span.quote: It is also important to mention that the term “exosomes” is often used to refer to the pellet obtained after 100,000× g ultracentrifugation. Although this pellet is probably enriched in exosomes, it might also contain small microvesicles as well as protein aggregates.

span.label: and the consequence is stated for the reader: changes in that pellet MAY NOT ONLY REFLECT CHANGES IN EXOSOME RELEASE, so a measured effect need not be about exosomes at all
span.quote: Therefore, one should be aware that changes in this pellet may not only reflect changes in exosome release.

span.label: THE STEPS CANNOT BE TOLD APART EXPERIMENTALLY: several molecules are implicated in ILV formation, MVB transport and MVB fusion, and `in many studies it is not clear at which step the investigated molecule/factor operates`
span.quote: Several molecules have been implicated in these processes, but due to methodological challenges, it is not easy to distinguish them experimentally, and in many studies it is not clear at which step the investigated molecule/factor operates

span.label: the purest available method still fails at the subtype level - density gradient centrifugation of the 100,000x g pellet `was not able to clearly separate subpopulations of small EVs`
span.quote: Moreover, Kowal et al. reported that density gradient centrifugation of 100,000× g pellets was not able to clearly separate subpopulations of small EVs

span.label: FINDING CONSENSUS IN THE FIELD IS COMPLICATED BY METHODOLOGICAL CHALLENGES - different isolation and quantification methods - which is the review's own closing verdict on why the literature disagrees with itself
span.quote: Finding consensus in the field is complicated by methodological challenges such as the use of different methods for exosome isolation and quantification.

span.label: the review devotes a section to methodological issues specifically BECAUSE they might explain discrepant findings, rather than reporting the literature as if it agreed
span.note: eliminates: a review that harmonises conflicting results by omitting the conflict · outcome: held
span.quote: The discrepant findings might be due to cell-specific regulations, or due to methodological challenges, such as different protocols for isolation of vesicles and different methods to quantify the amount of released exosomes

span.label: whether density gradient centrifugation - the purest available method - separates the subpopulations the subtype names claim
span.note: eliminates: nothing: Kowal et al. report it was NOT able to clearly separate subpopulations of small EVs · outcome: failed
span.quote: Moreover, Kowal et al. reported that density gradient centrifugation of 100,000× g pellets was not able to clearly separate subpopulations of small EVs

span.label: whether the several secretion routes - MVB, amphisome, lysosome - can be told apart by the extracellular product
span.note: eliminates: nothing: ILVs from an amphisome `will appear extracellularly as exosomes` and the pathways `share some features and do somewhat overlap` · outcome: failed
span.quote: Furthermore, when amphisomes fuse with the plasma membrane, the ILVs included in the amphisome will appear extracellularly as exosomes. Also if a lysosome secretes its content before it is fully degraded, remaining ILVs can be released as exosomes.

span.label: whether an implicated molecule can be assigned to ILV formation, MVB transport or MVB fusion
span.note: eliminates: nothing - in many studies it is not clear at which step the factor operates · outcome: failed
span.quote: Several molecules have been implicated in these processes, but due to methodological challenges, it is not easy to distinguish them experimentally, and in many studies it is not clear at which step the investigated molecule/factor operates

span.label: Exosomes
span.quote: Exosomes are nanosized membrane vesicles released by fusion of an organelle of the endocytic pathway, the multivesicular body, with the plasma membrane.

span.label: multivesicular body

span.label: small EVs
span.quote: In fact, it was recently suggested that this pellet should be referred to as small EVs (sEVs), since it was shown to contain different vesicle populations

span.label: EVs
span.quote: Three main types of EVs have been described based on their mechanism of release and size: exosomes (less than 150 nm in diameter), microvesicles/shedding particles and apoptotic bodies (both considered to be larger than 100 nm).

span.label: apoptotic bodies
span.quote: Three main types of EVs have been described based on their mechanism of release and size: exosomes (less than 150 nm in diameter), microvesicles/shedding particles and apoptotic bodies (both considered to be larger than 100 nm).

span.label: exosome, AS DEFINED IN THIS REVIEW: a vesicle released when a multivesicular body fuses with the plasma membrane. A DEFINITION BY ROUTE - the property is a history, not a feature of the object in hand
span.quote: Exosomes are nanosized membrane vesicles released by fusion of an organelle of the endocytic pathway, the multivesicular body, with the plasma membrane.

span.label: exosome, AS USED IN THE LITERATURE THIS REVIEW SURVEYS: the pellet from a 100,000x g spin. The two senses are in the same paper, two paragraphs apart, and the second is the one the experiments actually use
span.quote: It is also important to mention that the term “exosomes” is often used to refer to the pellet obtained after 100,000× g ultracentrifugation. Although this pellet is probably enriched in exosomes, it might also contain small microvesicles as well as protein aggregates.

span.label: small EVs (sEVs) - the replacement name proposed for that pellet BECAUSE it was shown to contain different vesicle populations. A term retreating from a claim about origin to a claim about size, which is what the measurement can support
span.quote: In fact, it was recently suggested that this pellet should be referred to as small EVs (sEVs), since it was shown to contain different vesicle populations

span.label: THE COINING, 1987, WITH ITS REASON: Rose Johnstone chose `exosome` because `the process seemed to be akin to reverse endocytosis`. The name was an analogy to a MECHANISM from the start, which is why it could never be settled by a measurement of the product
span.quote: Rose Johnstone, a pioneer in the field, chose the term “exosome” in 1987 because “the process seemed to be akin to reverse endocytosis, with internal vesicular contents released in contrast to external molecules internalized in membrane-bound structures

span.label: critiques → the practice of calling the 100,000x g pellet `exosomes`, on the ground that it also holds small microvesicles and protein aggregates and its changes need not be about exosome release
span.quote: It is also important to mention that the term “exosomes” is often used to refer to the pellet obtained after 100,000× g ultracentrifugation. Although this pellet is probably enriched in exosomes, it might also contain small microvesicles as well as protein aggregates.

span.label: critiques → studies assigning a molecule to a specific step of exosome biogenesis, on the ground that the steps are not easy to distinguish experimentally
span.quote: Several molecules have been implicated in these processes, but due to methodological challenges, it is not easy to distinguish them experimentally, and in many studies it is not clear at which step the investigated molecule/factor operates

span.label: supports → Kowal et al.'s finding that the small-EV pellet contains distinct populations, which motivates the retreat from `exosome` to `sEV`
span.quote: In fact, it was recently suggested that this pellet should be referred to as small EVs (sEVs), since it was shown to contain different vesicle populations

span.label: Exosomes —is-a→ EVs
span.quote: Three main types of EVs have been described based on their mechanism of release and size: exosomes (less than 150 nm in diameter), microvesicles/shedding particles and apoptotic bodies (both considered to be larger than 100 nm).
